The *Paṇḍaranāgarājajātaka* (Ja 518) is a canonical story in the Pali Jātaka collection within the Khuddaka Nikāya. According to the narrative setting, the Buddha related this story while residing at the Jetavana monastery in Sāvatthī in connection with Devadatta telling a lie and being swallowed up by the earth. In response to the monks' discussion of Devadatta's wrongdoing, the Buddha explained that Devadatta had also told lies and met the same fate of being swallowed by the earth in a previous existence, prompting this narrative of the past.
